items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I worked with George and I helped him with his instrument.

ctx.x: But he is so talented. He can just hear something and just fall right in, just a natural. He's just a natural.

But anyway, I worked with George and I helped him with his instrument. I didn't have much luck teaching him to read, but I did, you know, teach him chords and everything to play, the right chords and everything, and he was very, very attentive and paid close attention to everything, you know. But at that time he had a family, and I think that was maybe one of the reasons why he just didn't get in to study, you know. Like some people do, they just don't want to sacrifice the time. But he was a natural talent.

But anyway, we did very well on that job, and then at one time Monk MacVeal, Nathaniel MacVeal, worked on that job with me, and Lee, Lee Young worked there. He didn't work too much with me. He worked two or three nights. Dexter Gordon worked on that job once or twice with me. And before I went to work there, Lorenzo Flenoy had worked there, and I think Lorenzo worked there with a little trio or something, and then he got a bigger band and went on to something else, you know. So that's why -- I think that's why…
